nb_atomic_wall.blurb: Atomic Wall is the biggest of the faces at Sunnyside, outside Welsford in southern New Brunswick, roughly twenty minutes from Saint John by road. It holds 21 routes, nearly all of them bolted sport lines plus a single trad route. Grades run from 5.8 up to 5.11, with the bulk of the climbing between 5.8 and 5.10, so it suits climbers building up from moderate leads as well as those working harder lines. The wall is fairly steep for its grade range and sits just left of the main Sunnyside face. It is a compact crag, handy for a short session of several routes rather than a full-day objective.

nh_bonsai.blurb: Bonsai is a steep, much-visited wall in the West Crags of Rumney, New Hampshire. Of its 29 routes, most are bolted lines, with a handful of trad climbs and a few short ice routes in winter. Rock climbs span from an easy 5.4 or so through to 5.13, but the weight sits at the harder end, with the biggest cluster of routes in the 5.11 to 5.12 range and only a modest number of moderates. Expect sustained, pumpy climbing on large holds. The left side carries the harder test pieces while the right side offers friendlier grades. Tall pines at the base give shade in summer, and the wall is a regular stop for strong sport climbers.

nh_the_prudential.blurb: The Prudential is a destination wall in the northwest part of Rumney, New Hampshire, set a little away from the busiest cliffs, so it tends to be quieter. Most of its 29 routes are bolted sport lines, supplemented by a few trad climbs and one aid line. The wall is largely overhanging schist, with a honeycombed band that gives some lines a Red River Gorge flavor. Difficulty is concentrated at 5.11 and 5.12, with a smaller number of 5.8 to 5.10 routes and a couple of easy ones, so it rewards strong leaders more than beginners. The steeper right side dries quickly, which makes the crag a popular choice during wet spells.

nh_buffalo_pit.blurb: Buffalo Pit is a small but worthwhile cliff within the Rumney climbing area of New Hampshire, a short uphill stroll from its own lot beyond the main parking. It carries 29 routes, mostly bolted sport lines, with several trad climbs and one top rope. The range is unusually wide for a crag this size: a couple of beginner-level lines, a good group of 5.7 to 5.10 routes, and a solid block of 5.11 to 5.13 projects-turned-tests. The cliff was cleaned and developed heavily in recent years, so the rock is fresher than at older Rumney walls, and it is growing in popularity with both newer leaders and strong sport climbers.
